Order 
The applicant has filed this First bail application under Section 482 of BNSS/438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.

Applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No.267/2025 registered at Police Station Gola Ka Mandir District Gwalior (M.P.) in relation to the offence punishable under Sections 308(2),
308(6), 61(2) of BNS.

entities.text: Police Station Gola Ka Mandir District Gwalior
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the case of the prosecution, the complainant, Vivek Sharma, appeared at the police station along with his friend Manjesh Pachauri and lodged a verbal report stating that he owns two tractors.

He knows Sonu Gurjar, a resident of Himeyapura, Bijoli, Gwalior, presently residing at Deendayal Nagar, Adityapuram, for the past 6-7 months and had developed friendly relations through frequent telephonic conversations.
Sonu had earlier offered to arrange a girl for him if required, which the complainant declined.

On 02.08.2025 at about 8:00 PM, while the complainant was near Scindia Statue in his Scorpio car (Reg. No. MP-07-ZX-9142), Sonu called and, upon learning his location,
requested him NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7232 2 MCRC-9345-2026 to pick up a girl standing near Indraprastha Garden and drop her off, citing his own preoccupation.

Trusting him, the complainant reached the said location where a girl boarded his car after confirming that Pushpendra Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138188436/
1 Sonu had sent him.

sentences.text: She then directed him towards Govardhan Colony petrol pump, stating her sister was waiting there.

Before reaching the pump, two girls and two boys signaled him to stop;
upon halting, they forcibly entered his vehicle, turned it around, and upon reaching Gola Ka Mandir crossing, began accusing him of having committed sexual misconduct with the girl and threatened to file a rape complaint.

The complainant immediately informed his friend Manjesh Pachauri over phone that three girls and two boys, allegedly sent by Sonu Gurjar, were threatening to implicate him falsely, but his phone was soon snatched.
The girl who had initially boarded the car also joined in the false allegation, threatening to lodge a report under Section 376 IPC.

The group compelled him to drive towards City Centre and then the highway, restraining him from exiting the vehicle,
and demanded Rs.5,00,000/- to avoid implicating him in a criminal case.
Under duress, he contacted his friend Ranjeet Gurjar to come to the highway; however, his phone was again taken away.
They proceeded to Mansi Dhaba near Devaraj Hospital, where Sonu Gurjar joined them and reiterated the demand of Rs.5,00,000/-, threatening false criminal prosecution otherwise.
The complainant returned home, brought Rs.60,000/- in cash from his pocket, and handed it over to one of the boys.

They also took his car keys and his mobile phone (OnePlus Nord CE 3 Lite 5G; IMEI Nos. 862529060322398 and 862529060322380), containing Idea SIM No. 9826488413 and Jio SIM No. 9131587186, and thereafter abandoned his car at the spot before fleeing in an unidentified vehicle.
Subsequently, Ranjeet Gurjar arrived at the location along with the complainant's brother Rahul Sharma and driver Ramdas NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7232 3 MCRC-9345-2026 Singh.
Using the spare key brought by his brother, the complainant retrieved his car and returned home, narrating the entire incident to Ranjeet Gurjar, Manjesh Pachauri, and Rahul Sharma.
He alleged that Sonu Gurjar, in conspiracy with three unidentified girls and two boys, extorted Rs.60,000/-, his mobile phone, and car keys by putting him in fear of false criminal implication.

On the basis of this report, Crime No. 267/2025 was registered under Sections 308(2),
308(6), and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), and investigation was initiated.
It is submitted on behalf of the applicant that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The applicant has been arrayed as an accused solely on the basis of a memorandum statement recorded under Section 27 of the Indian Evidence Act at the instance of a co-accused person.
There is no independent or corroborative evidence connecting the applicant with the alleged offence, and his implication is wholly baseless and unjustified.

It is further submitted that the complainant has filed an affidavit clearly stating that he is acquainted with Pushpendra, the present applicant, as well as with Pooja Parihar, and neither the applicant nor Pooja Parihar has committed any incident or offence against him.
The applicant is a permanent resident of District Bhind and there is no likelihood of his absconding or evading the process of law.
He bears a good reputation and has no intention whatsoever to tamper with the prosecution evidence or influence any witness.
The applicant has fully cooperated with the investigating agency throughout and undertakes to extend full cooperation as and when required during the course of investigation and trial.
The applicant is ready and willing to abide by any terms and conditions that this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper to impose while granting the relief of anticipatory bail.
In view of the facts and circumstances stated hereinabove, it is prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and prayed for its rejection.
Learned counsel for the complainant submits that he has no objection to the grant of anticipatory bail to the present applicant.
Heard counsel for parties and perused the case diary.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.

Accordingly, it is hereby directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be enlarged on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for his appearance before it during the course of investigation or before the trial Court concerned during trial, as the case may be.
Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court/Police Station concerned for compliance.
Certified copy as per rules.
